results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

Audited all 121 mapped units, p001–p121, against the independent summaries in draft order: 12 introductory units, 101 body units across all 16 sections, and eight concluding units. The summaries preserve the contract’s progression from trust and shared platform surface through bounded reuse choices to evaluation and stewardship; shorter summaries such as p108 are supported by their attached risk/control evidence. The introduction callout is attached evidence with a null mapping, not an extra contracted paragraph.

Audited all 105 prose units, all 16 grouped list units, and the opening callout; the independent outliner flags no unit as carrying two ideas. The longer units remain unified: p030 defines the comparison’s technical terms, p057 makes one hardware/software analogy, p070 rejects three substitutes for the same decision rule, p097 enumerates one shared platform strategy, and p116 combines the prerequisites of sustainable ownership.

Audited every unit p001–p121, using section-level support where a paragraph inherits it. The trust discussion develops S1; the analogy and text-first surfaces develop S2; reuse and retained expertise develop S3; both worked cases develop S4; evaluation develops S5; platform policy, human responsibility, risks, and reflection develop S6. Introductory and concluding synthesis connects these claims, and p121 uses the S5/S6 responsibility for intended behavior to motivate its declared hand-off. No unit introduces an unrelated argument.

Audited all 71 declared evidence items across p001–p121 and the actual draft’s six tables, four figures and captions, three detached quotations, and other inline quotations and examples. The platform table is interpreted by the sufficient-capability condition in p031; the text-first table by visible composition in p039; the wheel table by the bounded judgment and acceptance questions in p053–p056; the economics table by the contextual choice in p082; the evaluation table by the spec/implementation/evaluation explanation in p089; and the risk matrix and Figure 4 by the safeguards and whole-system ownership analysis in p109–p112. The historical analogy, frontend and messaging scenarios, and quoted decision questions have explicit argumentative roles rather than being left as unexplained evidence. This assesses explanation and relevance, not external factual verification of the preserved historical or product claims.

Audited all 103 within-container paragraph boundaries and all 17 container boundaries against their declared relationships and carried-over ideas, including the concluding hand-off. The text carries trust cost into the RISC response, qualifies visible files with imported dependency behavior, moves from the frontend case to messaging’s failure handling, synthesizes both cases in p078–p080, connects judgment to evaluation at p084, and turns reuse criteria into shared rules at p096. Contrast, elaboration, example, emphasis, cause/effect, and summary relationships are present throughout; p116 has an independently reported wording problem, but its connection to the preceding trust/ownership cost remains the specified elaboration.

Audited the declared post-level problem/solution progression, its prerequisite, comparison, and small-to-large sequences, and every section’s local order against both independent flow accounts. Both readers correctly reconstruct why every section occurs where it does, including the economic synthesis after the cases, evaluation before policy, responsibility before risks, reflection before synthesis, and the final product hand-off. They recommend retaining the order and report no other lost connection; the one shared sentence-level hesitation is recorded separately below.

results.quote: Specifying behavior and exposing changes help only when the platform leaves evaluation and human ownership possible as output grows.
results.finding: Both independent flow readers reread this sentence because “leaves evaluation and human ownership possible” is abstract; the second could not initially tell whether it meant permission to perform those activities or keeping the growing system manageable enough to perform them. State the intended ongoing ability to test, review, and maintain the growing system directly; the surrounding synthesis and section order can stay.
results.corroborated_by: flow-reader-1.txt, Issue 1, and independently flow-reader-2.txt, item 1: both quote this exact Final Thought sentence and identify the same ambiguous phrase as the reason for rereading.

results.finding: Audited first uses and paragraph openings throughout p001–p121, including the explanatory terms expressly required by the contract’s evidence instructions. RISC, the platform instruction-set analogy, observability, blast radius, CPU opcodes, SaaS/API/ORM/CI, DRY, DOM, outbox/inbox, idempotency keys, contract/property/regression/golden tests, messaging failure terms, mechanical sympathy, mutation/fault tests, and blessed primitives receive explanations before the argument depends on their specialized meaning. Both flow readers find those definitions sufficient. The supplied post spec has no separate audience knowledge list; this verdict concerns the observed prerequisite dependencies and requested glosses in the supplied prose.

Audited the callout and all introduction units p001–p012. The opening asks a specific consequential question about trusting generated systems, explains the actual trust mechanism, bounds the RISC analogy, states the conditional thesis, and supplies a concrete roadmap. It is not a placeholder, a mere restatement of the essay question, a dictionary opening, a sweeping historical opening, or a book report.

Audited all eight Final Thought units p114–p121. The conclusion develops the combined role of boundaries, inspectability, evaluation, and ownership, gives a concrete platform-selection course of action, and limits the next-post contrast to its explicitly contracted hand-off. It does not reveal its thesis for the first time, rely on sentiment, import body evidence, or finish with a rephrased thesis alone; the local wording failure in p116 does not make the ending one of the enumerated weak patterns.

Audited p114–p121 against the synthesis, so-what, and takeaway contract. The conclusion combines the changed production/trust economics with stable boundaries, inspectable platforms, evaluation, and continuing human ownership rather than merely repeating one section. Its actionable selection rule in p120 explains the payoff as work the team understands and maintains instead of a growing review burden; the abstract phrasing in p116 is separately identified by the flow check.

Audited p114–p121 against callback.to and callback.how. The contrast between falling production cost and slower improvement in trust cost returns to the opening questions about how much code can be generated and how much can be trusted; p116 reconnects stable boundaries to dependable behavior, while p120 answers the opening with a reliable-platform choice and retained expertise rather than an output-volume target.

Compared the introduction-only reader’s predictions with all 16 body sections, the complete roadmap, and the conclusion. The reader predicts reviewer questions, the concrete instruction-set comparison and coding tools, dependency risks and reuse criteria, frontend and messaging examples, economic synthesis, evaluation, shared strategy, the human role, risks, and local reflection in their actual order. The predicted qualified historical analogy, practical examples, comparisons, and practitioner tone match the draft; the reader correctly does not claim the introduction promises measured case studies.

The independent AC-1 reader expands RISC correctly, explains the analogy as a deliberately smaller and more regular software surface shared by agents and human reviewers, names frameworks, libraries, APIs, conventions, tools, and dependencies, and recognizes that this surface changes over time. The answer also preserves the mature-expertise and sufficient-capability qualification, satisfying the criterion’s shared-understanding outcome.

The independent AC-2 reader allows a narrow helper only when behavior and edge cases are understandable and testable, failure is local and recoverable, and maintenance is owned. The reader retains mature security-sensitive implementations for expertise, difficult edge cases, standards, and operational experience, and explicitly compares total burden and reliability rather than line count or generation speed.

The independent AC-3 reader identifies platform stewardship, shared primitives and examples, review rules, ownership of repeated or growing local code, specs, meaningful tests, runtime visibility, and whole-system review including operations and rollback. The answer accounts for sprawl, fragmentation, false confidence, missed safeguards and edge cases, and complexity moved out of the code; it correctly leaves project-specific thresholds to context.
